scale_noun_agrees.source: No Frisian source on this was read: the value follows Dutch, CLDR RBNF nl (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, nl.xml), %spellout-cardinal: "1000000: ←← miljoen[ →→]". A native speaker must confirm it.

joiner_tens_units.source: Wiktionary, "ienentweintich": the unit comes before the ten

unit_ten_one_word.source: Wiktionary writes "ienentweintich" (21) as one word. No Frisian spelling rule was read; the value follows Dutch, where the rule is written (Team Taaladvies (Vlaamse overheid), "Aaneenschrijven - 07. Getallen, telwoorden en breuken", regel 1: "Schrijf getallen in woorden aaneen tot aan het woord duizend. Schrijf achter het woord duizend een spatie." ("32: tweeëndertig", "101: honderdeen of honderdeneen", "1001: duizend en een of duizend een", "3254: drieduizend tweehonderdvierenvijftig")).

bare_hundred_after_scale.source: "hûndert" names 100 alone, so after a group of thousands it starts the next group: Wiktionary, "hûndert": "Unlike English, the word hûndert means 'one hundred' by itself"

ten_joins_unit_ordinal.source: The ordinal 13th is one word, "trettjinde", so "ten" and a unit ordinal are two numbers: ovos-number-parser numbers_fy.py (a lead; no Frisian dictionary entry was checked for this word)

ordinal_joiner_by_place.source: An ordinal takes the joiner that the cardinal word in its place takes. Between a ten and a unit (never): Wiktionary, "ienentweintich": the unit comes before the ten After a hundred (never): No source read: the value follows the parser (ovos-number-parser numbers_fy.py (a lead; no Frisian dictionary entry was checked for this word))

comma_between_classes.source: No source read (ovos-number-parser numbers_fy.py, a lead) writes no comma between two classes. No source opened shows a comma between two classes of one number, so a comma ends a number.
